Chapter 7: The Weight of Forgiveness.
You know, forgiveness is one of those words folks throw around all the time, but actually living it? That’s a whole different story. When the truth about Daisuke’s past finally came to light, Rie found herself tangled up in emotions she could barely name. There was anger. Sadness. Even confusion. All those feelings swirled together, making it tough to figure out what she should do next.
Some days, she’d sit and replay every moment of their life together, trying to spot clues she might’ve missed. Other days, she’d feel a strange sort of gratitude for the happiness they’d shared—even if it was built on shaky ground. Friends and family tried to help: “Move on,” they said, or “Just forgive.” But none of it really felt right. Rie started to realize that forgiveness isn’t something you can just force. It doesn’t happen on anyone else’s timeline.
And Kido? He found himself thinking a lot about what forgiveness truly means. He’d seen families fall apart over secrets, friendships end in betrayal. But he’d also witnessed people find peace in the most unlikely places—choosing to forgive, not because it was easy, but because it was the only way to keep moving forward.
One quiet afternoon, Rie sat with her son in the park, just watching him play under that big, endless sky. She couldn’t help but think about the man who had been a father to her boy—the laughter, the gentle comfort, the little joys they’d shared. And it hit her: whatever had gone wrong, those memories were real. The love they’d felt wasn’t erased by everything that came after.
Forgiveness, she came to understand, wasn’t about excusing what Daisuke had done. It was about recognizing how complicated people’s choices can be, and the hurt that sometimes lies behind them. It meant letting go of the hope for perfect answers, and learning to honor the good that existed, right alongside the bad.
The truth is, most of us carry wounds that never fully go away. Forgiveness doesn’t often show up in grand gestures—it sneaks in during the smallest moments. Maybe it’s a kind word. Or a memory shared. Or just a quiet acceptance of things we can’t change.
For Rie, forgiveness gradually became less about Daisuke and more about herself. It was about reclaiming her own story—choosing to move forward, without letting the past keep her trapped. And that, in its own quiet way, was where healing started.
